## Merge and production preflight — 2026-10-04 00:26 UTC, Codex/root

GitHub refresh: 110 open PRs, 109 drafts; 49 target `main`, 61 target other PR branches, and nine are `DIRTY`/conflicting. The only non-draft is #834, based on `main`; it is `DIRTY`, with required Typecheck/Lint/Test/Build, Mobile, and Database jobs failed while E2E passes. Do not merge the batch or promote a draft as release-ready. The current Vercel CLI `whoami` attempt exits with `unable to verify the first certificate`, and this audit checkout has no Vercel project link. Production deployment status therefore cannot be confirmed or safely changed from this environment.

Exact-head #918 review (head `3d0c49cc0473d5cf43870d9040570c4f69a9cdee`, stacked on #913) found four release-blocking gaps. The family boundary is source-derived: an authenticated owner can write an arbitrary `sync_external_mappings.local_id`, and service-role folding reads/updates the target event by ID without family/calendar scope; the two-family database repro was not run. Changed-master-only pulls can overwrite previously folded exception slots. Overlapping syncs can lose disjoint slots through read-merge-write without serialization. String Set dedupe treats equal instants such as `...+00:00` and `....000Z` as different; JS equality behavior was checked, but a PostgREST round-trip was not. Current fake/in-memory tests and migration SQL probe do not cover these paths. Keep #918 unmerged until family-scoped reads/writes, durable date reconciliation, concurrency control, and timestamp normalization have executable coverage.

Isolated #890 commit `7a951926c0908abcd64bb50b4928c60a343c3b8a` is on exact PR head `610c4235f2f3e6bb67adaa31245576a70c6097b8`; synthetic PG17 fresh migration/runtime and both cleanup/adoption orderings pass, as do focused tests (6 files/99 tests), 8 GB TypeScript, migration audit, and diff checks. It remains local pending independent review and hosted checks. Isolated #906 commit `860cc529fdbad48f7e23e0e3ad290f4eecc2843e` is based on exact PR head `0b5e28d593766ecf48fc09d2a7e1f8ffb50abcb3`; 15 focused tests, targeted ESLint, 8 GB TypeScript and diff check pass. Materially different calendar details or budget amount/period now fail closed on natural-key replay, and malformed/legacy receipts without inputs do not report success. The promised later-budget-step-wins behavior remains unresolved; safely ordering/coalescing steps crosses approval/binding semantics. Both candidates remain local only. - Independent meal review (2026-10-03 15:07 UTC): On exact #897 head `084d1353`, `planWeek` writes created meals to the shared library before the atomic planning RPC and deletes them if a later entry fails resolution. A concurrent successful plan can start referencing one of those meals before the first request's cleanup deletes it; `meal_plans.meal_id` has `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so the committed plan silently loses its meal reference. Request-ID validation also occurs after library writes. AutoPlan UI/route pass no stable request key, while service fallback generates a new UUID, so a retry after commit with a lost HTTP reply can replace the week again. The test called “lost RPC response” asserts there were no plan table writes and does not cover commit-then-lost-response. Current exact-head #897 checks: Database and meal-plan SQL pass, Main fails, Mobile passes, E2E pending; #890 Database, E2E and Main fail while meal-plan SQL and Mobile pass. Findings remain open; no new acceptance or audit credit.

## Cron boundary bootstrap gap — 2026-10-03 16:33 UTC, Codex/root

On PR #902 exact head `ad19f27092bce3e5c625ccb986352ec5a6307e14`, the boundary lookup filters to successful scheduled runs, then treats an empty result as the first tick. The same empty response occurs if earlier scheduled runs exist but all failed or were cancelled, so a recovered tick can dispatch only its fixed five-minute window and finish green; if schedule deliveries were missed while no successful boundary existed, that tick becomes the next boundary and the gap is not recovered. The current empty-history tests do not distinguish first-ever execution from failed-only history because the API filter removes failures. This reproducible source/test gap was published at [#902](https://github.com/NewWorldVenture/Bubaly/pull/902#issuecomment-5971121597); requested a failed-only history regression and fail-closed boundary handling after dispatch. No branch changes. Current exact-head checks: Database, Mobile and Vercel pass; Main and E2E remain in progress; Supabase Preview skipped.

An independent reviewer confirmed the classification hole with synthetic scheduled `failure` and `cancelled` runs plus the current in-progress run: filtering the query to successful outcomes produces the same empty array as a true first run, which the code labels `lookup=ok`. The reviewer also found the `only this run` fixture labels its in-progress current run as successful; this does not invalidate the separate empty-array finding, but the fixture should be made realistic. GitHub REST documents the workflow-run status filter and conclusion values [here](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs?apiVersion=2026-03-10). No branch or ledger changes by the reviewer.

## Independent #890 race review — 2026-10-04 00:11 UTC, Codex/root

Independent read-only review found a second lifecycle race beyond same-name concurrent creation. In ordinary `planWeek`, `resolveEntries` may commit a new custom dish through `meal_ensure_custom` (`lib/services/meals/index.ts:318`) before all entries are resolved. If a later recipe lookup fails, `removeCreatedMeals` (`:481`) deletes that earlier meal. Between those operations, another writer can reuse the meal and commit its own `meal_plans` row; deleting the meal sets that other row's `meal_id` to NULL (`supabase/migrations/0002_tables.sql:229`). This can silently corrupt a successfully committed meal slot. Existing candidate concurrency proof races ordinary ensure against delegated replacement, not this failure-and-cleanup interleaving. The synthetic PG17 candidate's prior SQL/notes/rollback proof remains valid but does not cover this scenario. Root sent the exact interleaving to the isolated author; add a deterministic regression and ownership-safe cleanup before commit. - **TIME-003 finding: a title-only reminder edit moves the saved instant outside UTC (owner-account comment posted 2026-10-02 11:43 UTC, [#771 comment 5951639694](https://github.com/NewWorldVenture/Bubaly/pull/771#issuecomment-5951639694); read-only).**
  - **Mechanism, verified on main `01b2c380`:** the reminders-module blob is `296a2ec7`.
    - The edit field is filled with `reminder.remind_at.slice(0, 16)`, a UTC wall clock.
    - Save parses it with `new Date(remindAtRaw).toISOString()`, which reads it as device-local time.
  - **Reproduction:** the root's frozen receipt 0bf3f4 confirms author b45251. Each title-only Save shifts the instant by the device offset:
    - New York in October: 16:00Z → 20:00Z → 00:00Z the next day.
    - New York in December: 16:00Z → 21:00Z → 02:00Z the next day.
    - Tokyo: 16:00Z → 07:00Z → 22:00Z the previous day.
    - UTC does not drift. Cancel, an explicit refusal and a zero-row acknowledgment keep the original.
    - These are 7 characterization and control cases across 3 affected scenarios, not 7 workflow passes. This is a synthetic fixture; nothing about a deployed server, Auth, RLS or providers is claimed.

## Integrations — the 80 INTEGRATION rows (every external host) — 2026-09-28

*Claude session_01776xJyhVe8xJQvTGeNfT9T. Read on main at `7cf84171`.*

Each host was located in shipped code (`app`, `components`, `lib`, `shared`, `mobile`, `middleware.ts`, `next.config`) by a tree scan and classified by what the code does with it:
- **22 are called by the server.** Every outbound server `fetch` in `lib/`, `app/api` and `shared/` was enumerated, and every one carries a deadline, through `fetchWithDeadline`, `fetchWithTimeout` or its own signal. APNs uses HTTP/2 with its own timer.
- **No provider key reaches the browser.** The only `NEXT_PUBLIC_` values are the Supabase URL and anon key, the app and site URLs, the VAPID public key, the Stripe publishable key and build ids.
- **The rest** are CSP allow-list entries, image hosts, calendar URL patterns, share and retailer deep links, documentation links, and development sentinels.

Result: **76 ✅ PASS, 3 🛠 FIXED + PASS, 1 🔄 IN PROGRESS** (the owner's call).

| ID | Finding | Severity | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **INT-M01** | The fetcher for family-supplied URLs (calendar feeds, weekend feeds, the social-feed page reader) could be steered to an internal address by DNS rebinding. | Medium | `fetchPublicText` resolved a hostname and refused private answers, then called `fetch(hostname)`, which resolved it again. A zero-TTL answer could pass the check as public and connect as `127.0.0.1` or `169.254.169.254`, on every redirect hop too. Recorded earlier as "Recorded, not fixed: DNS rebinding". The document fetcher already pinned its socket; this one did not. | **Fixed:** `pinnedPublicFetch` resolves, applies the same address policy, and hands the socket that exact address through `lookup`. The hostname is kept for Host and TLS, there is no pooled connection, `Accept-Encoding: identity`, and http or https. It is the default for every caller. `tests/a-public-fetch-connects-where-it-checked.test.ts` runs real sockets with a stub resolver: the rebinding second answer is refused and never connected (red on the old fetcher), the pinned address is used with the hostname in Host, and private literals are refused. |
| **INT-L01** | Two buttons opened an external site in a new tab with no `noopener`, handing it `window.opener` (reverse tabnabbing): the contacts "open in Maps" and the profile's "Rate the app". | Low | `window.open(url, '_blank')` in `components/modules/contacts-module.tsx` and `profile-module.tsx`. Links elsewhere carry `rel="noreferrer"`. | **Fixed:** both pass `'noopener,noreferrer'`. `tests/an-external-tab-gets-no-handle-back.test.ts` holds it tree-wide (red on the old tree). |
| **INT-O01** | "Rate the app" on the profile opens the App Store's front page, not a Bubaly listing. | Low | `window.open('https://apps.apple.com/', …)`; the repository holds no App Store id, so there is no listing to link. | **Owner's call:** link a listing once one exists, or change the row. Left in place rather than hidden. |

## Storage audit — five buckets through the real Storage API — 2026-09-28

*Claude session_01776xJyhVe8xJQvTGeNfT9T. Local stack at `0463`.*

The boundary probes read `storage.objects` policies in SQL. They cannot see the three things that decide a real request: the bucket's `public` flag (served without RLS), its MIME allow-list, and the LIST endpoint. `scripts/api-audit/storage.mjs` drives the HTTP API a browser uses. It makes a parent, that parent's child, and a parent of another family, then tries every bucket as each of them and as a signed-out caller. It cleans up after itself and refuses any target but a local stack.

**Result: 54/54 OK.** The five STORAGE rows that were NOT STARTED move to ✅ PASS:
- **Where uploads may go.** Uploads land only in your own folder: `<user id>/` for `avatars`, `feedback-attachments` and `marketplace-photos`; `<family id>/` for `documents`.
- **Who else can touch an object.** Another family, the owner's own child and a signed-out caller cannot upload there, list it, overwrite it or delete from it. An HTML upload is refused by every MIME-restricted bucket.
- **`marketing-assets`** is the service role's alone.
- **`documents` and `feedback-attachments`** are private: their public URL is not served.
- **`avatars` and `marketplace-photos`** serve any object to anyone holding its URL. That exposure is declared, and their names are 122 random bits.

**Two expectations corrected on the way:**
- A public bucket also serves the object through the authenticated download API, not only the public path. That is the same exposure, not a second one, and the script records it as such.
- `marketplace-photos` keeps the shape SEC-001 closed for family media: a photo on a circle-only listing stays fetchable by anyone who kept its URL after leaving the circle. This is recorded for the owner, not changed.

**Made permanent:**
- `tests/the-audit-harness-refuses-a-non-local-target.test.ts` runs every script under `scripts/api-audit/`, plus `page-audit-session.mjs`, against a production URL and requires the refusal. It is red if any script's guard is removed.
- `family-media` (STORAGE-EA481A772907) stays with SEC-001's session.

**ROLE rows: all 61 read (49 ✅ PASS, 11 🛠 FIXED + PASS, 1 🔄 IN PROGRESS on ROLE-SCOPE-001, the owner's decision).** Each was read in full. The same-origin redirect helper was re-probed with 14 more hostile strings, and none left the origin. The local stack confirmed that an email change stays pending until confirmed, so nobody can edit their session's email onto the super-admin allowlist. The child-login throttle is backed by a per-IP limit. Every test file that names these files passes: 45 files and 686 tests for the eleven smaller modules, then 17 files and 163 tests for the next five. The billing columns on `families` and the `subscriptions` table are not writable by a parent (measured), so the trial cannot be self-extended. The last 32 (the auth pages, the auth and App Lock components, the session helpers, the mobile auth files and the operator scripts) added ROLE-L04 to -L08 below, and I18N-011, which is recorded OPEN rather than fixed because it spans 689 call sites. The App Lock is a curtain by design (`lib/security/app-lock.ts`): its salted hash is in the page and a reload resets the cooldown; the session and RLS are the boundary.

## DB-RPC pass — every function in `public`, who may call it and what it checks — 2026-09-28

*Claude session_01776xJyhVe8xJQvTGeNfT9T. Local Supabase with every migration through `0463`.*

**What was checked.** The inventory listed 77 functions (DB-RPC-001…077). The database holds **127**, not counting extension functions, including the two added here. The 50 with no row are added as DB-RPC-078…127, and every row now carries its facts.
- **SECURITY DEFINER:** 91 functions, 62 callable and 29 triggers. **Every one pins its `search_path`.** The 36 invoker functions run with the caller's own rights; the 7 among them without a `search_path` are pure functions or triggers that read nothing outside their row.
- **Who may EXECUTE:** 16 definer functions are the service role's only. 14 are callable by `authenticated` only. 32 are callable by `anon` too, because Supabase's default privileges grant every new function to `anon` directly. Each of those reads the caller in its body, directly or through a helper, and signed-out callers are refused. The exceptions are `public_stats` and `public_handled_stats`, the marketing site's platform-wide counts, deliberately public and allowlisted by `definer-functions-check-their-caller-check.sql`.
- **Bodies read:** every callable definer function that no probe exercised. The wallet functions (`wallet_transfer`, `wallet_decide_allowance`, `wallet_decide_spend`), `move_recalculate_date`, `vacation_import_confirmation` (whose idempotent retries re-authorise), `marketplace_complete_handoff`, `marketplace_decline_offer` and `rate_limit_hit` each check the actor, the role and the family before acting.
  - `document_object_is_restricted` lets `anon` ask whether a sensitive document sits at an exact storage path. The path carries two uuids, so this is recorded, not changed.
- **Two defects found and fixed in the repository:**

| ID | Finding | Severity | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DB-RPC-M01** | A family that could not see a marketplace listing could still bid on it, Buy-It-Now it, open a negotiation on it, and file an offer that moved it to "pending". It needed nothing but the listing's id, which is in every item URL a circle member shares. | **High** | Measured as a parent of a family in no circle the listing was shared with, who could SELECT 0 of the 2 listings. `marketplace_place_bid` → `{"ok": true, "leading": true}`. `marketplace_negotiation_offer` → ok. `marketplace_buy_now` → ok: the listing became `claimed` with a confirmed order naming the outsider. `insert into marketplace_offers` landed, and the SECURITY DEFINER trigger `marketplace_offer_flip_pending` moved the listing to `pending`. ## DB policy pass — every table's RLS, every policy's caller — 2026-09-28

*Claude session_01776xJyhVe8xJQvTGeNfT9T. Local Supabase with every migration through `0461`.*

**What was checked.** For all 492 tables in `public`:
- **RLS:** enabled on every one.
- **Tables with no client policy:** 58. Every client is refused there and only the service role reaches them: the marketing, rate-limit, webhook, token and settings tables. That is the intended shape.
- **Policies:** all 1,073 permissive policies a client role can use (`anon`, `authenticated` or PUBLIC) were read. Each was judged on the expression that governs its command, `USING` for reads, updates and deletes, `WITH CHECK` for inserts. That expression names the caller in every case: `auth.uid()`/`auth.jwt()`, or a call to one of 67 public helpers whose body reaches the caller directly or through another helper (`is_family_member`, `can_manage_family`, `social_has_permission`, `is_marketplace_circle_member`, …).
- **Exceptions:** 13 policies are deliberately public: published marketing pages and Q&A, the blog, and catalogues every family shares. None sits on a table with a `family_id`. One policy is `USING (false)`, which admits nobody.

**Result: no table admits a caller it cannot identify.** A-16 (`blanket-policy-check.sql`) only forbids a literal `true`, so a policy like `using (status = 'open')` on family rows would have passed CI. This pass is the first check that would catch it.

**Made permanent:** `docs/audit/every-policy-names-its-caller-check.sql`. CI's Database job runs it, since the runner globs `*-check.sql`.
- **Derived helper set:** the caller helpers come from `pg_proc`, iterated to a fixed point, so a new helper counts the day it lands.
- **Negative control:** in a rolled-back transaction it creates a family table with a leaky `using (status = 'open')` policy and a tied one, and requires the detector to flag exactly the leaky one.
- **Allowlist checks:** it fails on a stale allowlist entry, or on an allowlisted policy that sits on family data.

**What it does not prove.** It checks that each policy names who is asking, not that the rule is the right one. For example, API-SWEEP-06 read half (a child reads the family's `transactions`) passes, because `is_family_member(family_id)` names the child. That remains the owner's decision.

**Register movement.**
- All 490 NOT STARTED DB-TBL rows move to 🔄 IN PROGRESS, each carrying its RLS state, its policy counts per command and whether it is family-scoped. What remains is per-role expectations and the workflows that use each table.
- DB-TBL-161 (`guardian_communications`), already in progress, has the result appended.
- `push_deliveries` had no row and is added as DB-TBL-492.
- Register B: **14,230 = 12,690 NOT STARTED + 1,478 IN PROGRESS + 52 FIXED + PASS + 1 PASS + 9 BLOCKED + 0 FAIL.**

**Also reconciled.** Fifteen findings in the Pass D/E/F summary tables still said OPEN although the code had fixed them: F-E02…F-E08, F-F03, F-F09, F-D01, F-D02/03 and F-G09. Each now states what the current code does and which file or migration did it. Twelve are fixed, four of those only in the repo until the operator applies their migrations. F-E02 is partial: step-up is enforced in RLS only for the budget and the vault. F-E06 is fixed as far as the repo can go.

*session_01DXw2nu25BjyRfA6Fg3YiMS. Local stack, a production build of main at `beb2de2b`, then of the fix.*

- The balance is summed from a paged read of the child's whole ledger, which fails closed past its ceiling. The history list stays the newest 200, and is listed, never summed.
- `tests/a-child-wallet-balance-is-the-whole-ledger.test.ts` runs the page itself over a store capped at 1,000 rows a read. It is red on the previous code (1,386 of 8,400 invested cents).
- Retested in the browser: the parent and the teen both see $96.34, with Invest at $85.23.
- Every other place that sums the ledger (treasury, send, goals, invest, the AI wallet routes, the admin console) was checked; each already reads the whole ledger in pages.

Recorded in full as DATA-023 under High Priority. Production readiness is unchanged: **NO**.

## API sweep — every route under app/api, four callers — 2026-09-27

*Claude session_01776xJyhVe8xJQvTGeNfT9T. Register B's API rows, which no one had claimed.*

**What was run.** Every method of every `app/api/**/route.ts` (155 route methods in 147 files, discovered from disk) was called against a local production build of `main` at `25a3a808` (Next 16.3.6) and a local Supabase with every migration through `0458`. Each was called as four callers: signed out, a `child` member, a non-admin parent, and a parent who is a super admin (`scripts/api-audit/sessions.mjs`, which creates both parents through the real sign-in form and onboarding). Each call sent the input a careless or hostile client sends: nothing on a GET, and on a POST an empty JSON object and a body that is not JSON (`scripts/api-audit/sweep.mjs`, 1,008 calls). `scripts/api-audit/summarize.mjs` puts every call in one bucket:

- **FAIL**: a 5xx, a dropped connection, a stack trace or database error text in the body, an `/api/admin` route answering 2xx to a child or non-admin parent, or a cron route answering anything but 401/403 without the cron secret.
- **BLOCKED**: a 503 that says the feature is not set up on this server.
- **REVIEW**: a 2xx to a signed-out caller or to a non-JSON body.
- **OK**: everything else.

**First sweep: 24 FAIL.**
- 7 were real 500s: the four AI routes `invest`, `relationship`, `wallet` and `weekly-briefing`; billing `checkout` and `portal`; and `google/calendar/auth` with an empty body.
- The rest were honest "not configured" 503s, counted as FAIL until the summariser learned to tell them apart.
- Reading the routes behind the 500s found three more defects than the sweep could see.

**After the fixes: 0 FAIL, 30 BLOCKED, 11 REVIEW, 114 OK.**
- All 30 BLOCKED routes answer an honest 503 because this build has no AI, Stripe, push, GIF or Twilio credentials.
- All 11 REVIEW routes were read. Each is a public read-only endpoint (`health`, `build-info`, `blog/search-index`, `services/descriptions`, `exit-intent/resolve`) or reads an optional body with `readBoundedRequestJsonOrEmpty`, which treats an unreadable body as empty on purpose.
- No admin route answered a child or a non-admin parent. No cron route ran without its secret. No response carried internal detail.

| ID | Severity | Route(s) | Problem | Fix | Test (red before the fix) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-SWEEP-01 | Medium | `GET /api/google/calendar/auth` | With no Google credentials, "Connect Google" on `/dashboard/calendar` threw and left the parent on a blank 500 page. | Returns the parent to the calendar with `gcal=not_configured` and a translated toast, as the Outlook link beside it already does. | `tests/google-calendar-connect-without-credentials.test.ts` |
| API-SWEEP-02 | **High** | `POST /api/billing/{checkout,portal,cancel,change-plan}` | Super Admin → Stripe Setup saves a secret key and promises "configured value first, then env", but only checkout honoured it. Portal, cancel and change-plan read `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` alone, so a family that subscribed through the configured key could not open the portal, cancel or change plan. With no key anywhere, all four answered 500. Checkout also built its client before reading the body, so a malformed body got a 500 instead of a 400. | All four resolve the key the same way (Setup, then env). Without one they answer 503 "billing isn't set up" before any Stripe call. Checkout reads the body first. | `tests/billing-uses-the-stripe-keys-the-admin-configured.test.ts` (8 of 10 cases red before) |
| API-SWEEP-03 | **High** | `POST /api/webhooks/stripe` | Read `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` alone and built a client with `getStripe()` just to check the signature. On a deployment whose key and secret live in Stripe Setup, that threw, and the catch answered "signature invalid" to every real event, so no subscription would ever be recorded. | The Setup secret first, then env, verified with Stripe's keyless static verifier (`constructWebhookEvent` in `lib/stripe.ts`). A wrong secret is still refused. | Same file, with real signatures from Stripe's own test-header generator |
| API-SWEEP-04 | Medium | 14 AI routes; `ai/health/coach` | With no AI key, 18 AI routes said "the engine isn't set up" (503). Nine let the provider's throw reach a generic catch (500). Four answered 502 "temporarily unavailable", which tells the family to retry when retrying cannot work. `ai/health/coach` checked only the environment, so a key saved in Admin → AI Engine was reported missing. | Each asks `isAIConfigured()` before calling the provider. Three routes keep their deliberate model-free fallback, named in the guard: `journal`, `savings` and `behavior/insight`. | `tests/an-ai-route-says-when-the-engine-is-not-set-up.test.ts` (15 of 31 red before) |
| API-SWEEP-05 | **High** (privacy) | `POST /api/ai/savings` | Answered a signed-in child with advice built from the family's transactions, budgets, unpaid bills and subscriptions. The finance service refuses non-managers ("Family finances are private to the adults in this family"), and the privacy export withholds `finances` from a child. | 403 for non-managers before any read. | `tests/a-child-is-not-given-the-familys-savings-advice.test.ts` (3 of 5 red before) |
| API-SWEEP-07 | Medium | invite, welcome, referral and admin re-send; `cron/weekly-digest`, `cron/chore-reminders` | Found by the cron pass (below): `weekly-digest` reported `{"sent":4}` on a server with no mail provider. `sendEmail`/`sendReactEmail` answer `{ ok: true, skipped: true }` without `RESEND_API_KEY`, a contract the contact form relies on. So every caller that read only `ok` called nothing sent "sent". The invite, welcome, referral and admin re-send flows told the person their email had gone. The two crons counted every skip as a send. (The notification digest was already safe: it stops before sending when email is off.) | Each caller reads `skipped`. The four person-facing flows answer their existing "couldn't send" message (the referral also rolls back its record). The crons count a skip as a skip. | `tests/an-email-that-was-not-sent-is-not-reported-sent.test.ts` (8 callers red before); `tests/an-invite-with-no-mail-provider-is-not-sent.test.ts` (the real `lib/email`, red before) |
| API-SWEEP-06 | **High** (privacy) — ⚠️ **OPEN (reads)**; writes 🛠 FIXED + PASS (0460) | database: `transactions`, `budgets`, `bills`, `subscriptions_tracked` | Found while tracing API-SWEEP-05. Probed with a child's own session against the local database: each table's SELECT policy is `is_family_member(family_id)`, so a child reads the family's budgets, bills and tracked subscriptions straight from the REST API. `subscriptions_tracked` also lets any member *write* (`Members manage subscriptions_tracked`, command `*`). Migration 0267 guards only the writes on the first three. The app treats finances as adults-only in three places, and the database does not. | **Write half fixed** (session_01TRY21ZKsFrfB3qtoP972A4, 2026-09-28): `0460_a_child_cannot_rewrite_the_familys_subscriptions.sql` drops 0076's `FOR ALL` "Members manage subscriptions_tracked" and makes insert, update and delete `can_manage_family`, the 0267 shape; reads stay `is_family_member`. Page audit B11 had watched a PIN child add a family subscription. Checked on the local stack as that child: "Add subscription" answers "You don't have permission to do that…" and writes nothing, and the parent's add still says "Added". Needs the operator's production migration step like every schema change (PROD-DB-0177). **Read half not fixed.** A manager-only SELECT policy is the obvious fix, but the home page, wallet hub, voting, briefing and agent readers also read these tables. It needs the owner's decision on what a child may see, then a migration, then those readers checked. Production application of any migration is the owner's (PROD-DB-0177). | Writes: `docs/audit/a-child-cannot-rewrite-the-familys-subscriptions-check.sql`. It runs as a real child session, with a negative control (the same child makes all four writes in a household they manage) and a check on the whole policy set. It fails before 0460 on both the policy check and "1: a child added a family subscription", and passes after. Reads: a probe asserting a child JWT reads zero rows, still to write when the owner decides |
| API-SWEEP-08 | Medium | `POST /api/email/invite` | Found by session_01KP9rt5rVQ9jDMpZp2xBy3K while retesting API-SWEEP-07's invite change on a local stack. `rate_limit_hit` (0179) raises when a signed-in caller's key does not name their own user id. This route keyed its bucket `email:invite:<familyId>` and evaluated it on the member's session client, so the RPC raised, the limiter failed closed, and every invite email answered 429. The invite form said, every time, that it could not send the invitation. | The family-wide bound is the route's stated intent and is kept. It is now evaluated on the service client, as every IP- and address-keyed public route already is. The invite read stays on the member's session. Retested live on a production build against a real invite row: the request passed the limiter, wrote the bucket (count 1) and reached the send, while the earlier builds answered 429. | `tests/a-signed-in-rate-limit-key-names-the-caller.test.ts` checks all 86 rate-limit calls in `app/` and `lib/`: any key not provably on the service client must name the caller. It flags exactly this route on the old code. |

## Page Audit — every page on www.bubaly.com

*Started 2026-09-27 on the owner's instruction: "go through every single page
on bubaly.com and audit to make sure each is working perfectly, with no
issues … allow other bots (Claude and Codex) to work simultaneously on this.
Make sure to fix everything uncovered before moving on."*

**What a row's status means, exactly.** This is a *page* audit, not a workflow
audit: ✅ CLEAN says the page renders correctly, not that every action on it has
been exercised end to end. That is why no `PAGE-` or `UI-ROUTE-` row above is
moved to PASS from here — those registers mean a full workflow verified, and
this section links to them instead of overwriting them.

A page is ✅ **CLEAN** when all three hold:

- **Signed out, production** (`scripts/page-audit/crawl.mjs` against
  https://www.bubaly.com, phone 375×812 and desktop 1280×800): the right answer
  for a visitor — the page itself for a public route, a redirect to `/login`
  for a signed-in one, a 404 for a dynamic route opened with an id that matches
  nothing — with no uncaught error, no console error, no failed or 4xx/5xx
  subresource, no horizontal overflow, and no axe WCAG 2.1 A/AA *serious* or
  *critical* violation. Every link found on a crawled page is also requested.
- **Signed in, local sweep** (`tests/e2e/every-page-signed-in.spec.ts`, run in
  CI's E2E job against the disposable Supabase; locally the same against
  `supabase start`): opened by a parent who is also a super admin, the page
  answers below 500 and not 404 (a dynamic route may 404 on its no-such-id
  path), throws nothing, logs no console error, renders no raw catalogue key,
  does not double the brand in its title and does not overflow 1280 px. The
  spec discovers routes from `app/**/page.tsx`, so a page added tomorrow is in
  it tomorrow.
- **Signed in, phone** (`scripts/page-audit/crawl.mjs` with `STORAGE_STATE`
  set to that signed-in session, 375×812, against the same local build): the
  signed-out crawl's checks — axe WCAG 2.1 A/AA *serious*/*critical*,
  overflow, uncaught and console errors, failed subresources — on the page a
  parent actually sees on a phone. Added after the desktop-only sweep had
  called 340 pages clean: at phone width every signed-in page failed axe on
  the shell (a nameless logo link, avatar initials at 4.46:1), and 55 pages
  had their own failures. A page is not clean until all three checks hold.

Other statuses: 🔧 **FIXED, NOT LIVE** (the defect is fixed in a named commit
that production does not serve yet), 🔧 **FIXED, LIVE — re-crawl pending**
(production serves the fix; the signed-out production crawl has not been
re-run on it, so the row is not yet called clean), ⚠️ **OPEN** (a defect is recorded and
not fixed, with the reason), 🔒 **OWNER** (the fix is the owner's — data, a
secret, a decision), 🔄 **CLAIMED** (someone is on it; see Claim).

### Working on this in parallel (Claude, Codex, anyone)

The 398 routes are split into six **lanes**. A lane is claimed as a whole, so
two sessions never edit neighbouring rows and their merges do not conflict.

1. `git fetch origin main` and read the **Lanes** table *on origin/main*, and
   the open PRs touching `finalaudit.md`. Take a lane whose Claim is empty or
   older than 12 hours.
2. Put your session id and the UTC time in that lane's Claim cell, commit that
   one line alone, and get it to `main` first (a claim nobody else can see is
   not a claim).
3. Work your lane's rows only: re-run the two checks for the rows you touch,
   fix what you find (the same rules as the rest of this audit — a failing test
   first, the fix, the test green, mutation-proved where it can be), update the
   row, and move it to 🔧 FIXED, NOT LIVE with the commit. After the release
   reaches production, re-crawl the route and move it to ✅ CLEAN.
4. Release the lane (clear the Claim) when you stop, finished or not.

Re-running the checks: `node scripts/page-audit/routes.mjs > paths.txt`, then
`node scripts/page-audit/crawl.mjs paths.txt out.jsonl 4` and
`python3 scripts/page-audit/summarize.py out.jsonl`; and
`E2E_AUTHENTICATED=1 npx playwright test tests/e2e/every-page-signed-in.spec.ts --project=chromium`
with the local Supabase credentials in the environment; and, for the phone
column, `STORAGE_STATE=state.json BASE=http://localhost:3107 VIEWPORTS=phone
node scripts/page-audit/crawl.mjs paths.txt out.jsonl 4` with a storage state
saved from a signed-in browser.

> is a duplicate grocery item"* has nothing to trip on until it is made.
>
> **The same question was then put to the TASK list, and it was stale too.**
> Six tasks read *"in progress"* or *"pending"* while the work behind them was
> either finished or blocked on the owner. Each was checked against
> `2026MarketDom.md`'s own per-phase *"Still open"* line rather than against its
> title:
>
> | task | what actually remains |
> |---|---|
> | Phase 1 — Unify | the `request_id` link the inbox cannot claim **without the §6 migration** |
> | Phase 2 — Automate | *"nothing in this phase without a migration"* — done to the agent-doable limit |
> | Phase 3 — Deepen | the replacement lineage, **§6 item 9** |
> | Phase 4 — Expand | M27 and M32, and M37's kiosk pairing — **§6 items** |
> | Public site | W7's second half, **§6 item 18** |
> | K2 referral flywheel | **nothing — it is done**, and was marked `pending` |
>
> So every phase's remainder is a migration §6 forbids an agent from creating.
> That is a materially different state from *"in progress"*, and it is recorded
> here because a task list that says "in progress" about work waiting on a
> human sends the next agent to re-do it.
>
> **Two corrections came out of checking rather than assuming.** The referral
> flywheel was verified before being closed — its three named tests exist and
> pass (45 assertions), `signup/actions.ts` really does capture and cookie the
> `?ref=` code, `onboarding/actions.ts:494-500` applies it as `signup_link`, and
> `rewardReferral` credits through `createBalanceTransaction` and no-ops on an
> already-`rewarded` row. And the Public site's *"still open"* translation pass
> **has quietly closed**: all six non-English catalogues now carry all 13,778
> keys against the 304 missing that line recorded. Checked for the way that
> number could lie — a catalogue padded with English — and it does not: 0–8% of
> values match `en-US` in the named groups, `ai.*` is 0%, and
> `pricingContent.after5Days` is *"Nach 5 Tagen"*, *"Après 5 jours"*,
> *"Passados 5 dias"*.
>
> So the finding rows are at the state an audit reaches on its own. What keeps
> **PRODUCTION READY: NO** is not those fifteen: it is the 22 Critical Blockers
> below, nearly all of which read *"deployed / hosted / real provider remains
> unverified"* and need a live environment, plus the fact that **none of
> `0318`–`0340` has been applied to production**.

> **Merge note (2026-09-20).** This file is the union of two audits that ran in
> parallel and have now been merged: the Codex cycle's control document, which
> leads and remains authoritative for the counts above, and the Claude audit
> branch's own consolidated file, preserved from *"# Bubaly — Final Audit"*
> onward along with its pass-by-pass evidence. Nothing was dropped from either;
> where they disagreed the rows say so.
>
> **The three ❌ FAIL rows as of this merge:**
>
> - **SEC-001** — the *cache* half is **fixed**: `public/sw.js` was serving one
>   account's private family photos to the next account on the same device, out
>   of a logout-surviving Cache Storage entry with no network request for the
>   server to deny. The *bucket* half is untouched and SEC-001 stays **FAIL** —
>   it needs provider configuration and a consumer migration to signed URLs, in
>   that order.
> - **AUTHZ-003** — **fixed** by `0319_social_access_delete_matches_grant.sql`
>   (unapplied). The repair had been written weeks earlier and was stranded on an
>   unmerged branch, which is why this document still carried it as FAIL.
> - **AUTHZ-005** — **fixed** by `0318_guardian_safety_config_is_manager_only.sql`
>   (unapplied). Written during this merge, because the no-SQL fence that blocked
>   it applies to *applying* migrations, not to writing one.
>
> **Applying** any migration remains a human action; none of `0318`–`0323` has
> been applied. See `docs/PENDING_PROD_MIGRATIONS.md`. `0321` must **not** be
> applied as written — it needs `create index concurrently`.
>
> **`0322` and `0323` (Pass BN) close eight more write boundaries**, and one of
> them — **AUTHZ-006** — is the sharpest finding of this cycle: `0318` held, and
> a child walked around it by writing the *suggestion* a `SECURITY DEFINER`
> function copies into the table they could not touch. The parent approved in
> good faith. See the rows in §3.
>
> ### ⚠️ WRITTEN IS NOT APPLIED, and every "closed" row below depends on it
>
> **None of `0318`–`0338` has been applied.** They exist as files in this
> repository and are proved against a replayed database; production has not
> seen one of them. So for every row in §3 that reads *"Fixed by 0322"* or
> *"closed by 0324"*, the accurate present tense is **fixed in the repository,
> open in production**.
>
> This matters beyond bookkeeping, because the Pass BR sweep classified a dozen
> manager-gated paths as **defeated** precisely *because* a migration in the
> tree closes their source table — `gift_payments` by `0322`, `pay_handles` and
> `wallet_goals` by `0324`, `dashboard_layouts` by `0325`. Read against
> production rather than against this tree, **those paths are live**, and the
> chains they sit in are exploitable today:
>
> - a child can still repoint a Pay ID and redirect a grandparent's payment
>   (**AUTHZ-010**);
> - a child can still author a savings goal that drains a sibling's balance on
>   a parent's click (**AUTHZ-009**);
> - a child can still rewrite the Guardian suggestion a parent approves
>   (**AUTHZ-006**).
>
> The repairs are real and tested. Until a human applies them, they protect
> nobody. `0321` additionally **must not** be applied as written — it needs
> `create index concurrently`. See `docs/PENDING_PROD_MIGRATIONS.md`.
>
> One finding was **withdrawn** in this merge rather than kept: **BK-01**
> (`allowance_rules` writable by the child it pays) was real and reproduced, but
> `main`'s `0306` had already closed it, better. That row records the mistake
> because the mistake generalises — absence from a failure list is not evidence
> that nobody looked.
>
> **Post-merge passes (2026-09-20), all pushed and CI-running on PR #541:**
>
> - **Pass BL** — the two i18n ratchets that went red at the merge. Neither had
>   been broken: each is one audit's instrument, newly aimed at the other's
>   code. Measured with one scanner held fixed over three trees (2,823 / 2,811 /
>   2,823), so the merge added nothing. Of the twelve findings this branch
>   contributed, **none was new untranslated copy**; six were removed on their
>   own merits and six are recorded as **I18N-006** rather than half-converted.
>   A measurement error is recorded with them: archiving without
>   `lib/i18n/messages/INVARIANT.txt` makes the scanner fall back to an empty
>   invariant set **in silence**, which pointed the first reading backwards.
> - **Pass BM** — `tests/no-route-gates-on-a-per-instance-limit.test.ts` caught
>   a half-fix of this audit's own. Pass BA found a service-role write above an
>   auth check and removed the durable rate limiter instead of relocating it;
>   the limiter is now after `resolveAssistantLink`, keyed on the principal.
>   Where that collided with `main`'s boundary guard, the reconciliation is
>   written down: the assertion that changed was a **proxy** for the boundary,
>   every assertion carrying the boundary itself is untouched, and two were
>   added.
>
> Also closed post-merge: the split cron counter, the blog unsubscribe banner,
> an ungated vacation-import endpoint, a photo lightbox that claimed
> `aria-modal` inertness with none of the behaviour, an object namer that
> invented `.jpg` for files of unknown type, and four workflows that
> contradicted `.nvmrc` — this box was running Node 22 against a repo that
> declares 24, which accounted for two apparent failures that were the runtime
> rather than the source.
>
> **Full suite on the declared Node 24.21.0: 1,348 files / 17,170 tests, all
> passing.** `tsc` clean, i18n gate clean, 334 migrations / 0 failed, 46/46
> boundary probes.
>
> **Still NO on production readiness**, and the three reasons are unchanged:
> SEC-001's bucket half, the unapplied migration ledger, and I18N-001.

## Critical Blockers

| # | Blocker | Why it cannot be resolved from the repository |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | **This branch's ten migrations (`0406`–`0418` less `0412`, `0413` and `0417`; renumbered from `0318`–`0330` in `C1-S9-89` and from `0361`–`0370` in `C1-S9-92`) are not applied to production** | Applying them needs operator credentials no agent in this audit has had. They include live privilege-escalation fixes. Listed in `docs/PENDING_PROD_MIGRATIONS.md`. |
| B2 | **No authenticated browser session** | There is no local Supabase, so `app/(app)` cannot be exercised as a signed-in user. Every authenticated-UI finding here is statically derived or driven through the in-memory Supabase fake. **2026-09-27: no longer true in every session.** The page-audit session ran `supabase start` (every migration to 0459, realtime off) and crawled all 393 signed-in routes as a signed-in parent and super admin at phone and desktop on local production builds, and CI's E2E job signs in against its disposable Supabase. What remains true: realtime was off locally, and the provider-backed workflows (email, SMS, OAuth, payments) are not exercised with live providers. |
| B3 | **The Expo app has never been run** | Read and typechecked only. |
| B4 | **Production schema never verified** | The audit replays migrations into a local PG17/16; whether production matches is unverified. |
| B5 | **No real screen reader, no `forced-colors`** | Accessibility findings are axe-derived plus static analysis. |
| B6 | **The `family-media` bucket remains public** | Session A found this as `F-E03` / `LB-009`; Session B tracks `SEC-001` at FAIL. The original six-consumer inventory below is historical: Q59 subsequently migrated consumers to signed reads. Incoming main contains that consumer work and the v5 optimizer/write fix; the September 27 cycle adds newly reproduced cache-read repairs. No deployed private-bucket access change or complete authorized/denied production readback has been verified. Consumer migration alone cannot enforce privacy while the bucket is public. **2026-09-27:** `0459` makes it private in the repository (retested locally: the stored public URL now answers 400, members read through signatures, another family is refused); production stays public until the operator applies 0459 (`docs/PENDING_PROD_MIGRATIONS.md`). |
| B7 | **This container runs Node 22.22.2; the repository declares 24.21.0** | `.nvmrc` and `engines.node` were bumped by the parallel session. `nvm` cannot fetch the Node 24 distribution from here, so `tests/node-version-is-pinned.test.ts` and `tests/stream-cancellation-runtime.test.ts` cannot pass locally. CI resolves Node from `.nvmrc`, so hosted runs use 24. Not counted as PASS. Audit `C1-S9-09`. |
| B8 | **Historical App Lock rollout blocker; the source fix has since merged** | `C1-S9-44` repaired the refused-preference-read bypass. The earlier statement that this fix was only on an unmerged branch was superseded when #556 merged, and it is included in current main06dd. Incoming hosted CI and exact public build identity are verified above. A public build check does not itself verify the complete authenticated App Lock workflow; that workflow remains subject to its individual audit record. |

*Per the brief: a BLOCKED item does not count as PASS, and while B1 affects
security-critical functionality the release gate stays NO.*

# Part 0 — the audit this control document sits on top of


# Part 0 — Consolidated index (authoritative)

*Rebuilt 2026-09-14 by Claude-1. This is the one current view; where an earlier
summary below disagrees with this part, this part is newer.*

*Merged 2026-09-14 with a second session that ran against this repository at the
same time and reached `main` first. Every finding from both sides is present —
120 distinct IDs, verified by set comparison across the merge, none dropped. Two
consequences are recorded rather than smoothed over: that session's rewrite
replaced **session record 1's index prose**, so only record 2 now survives
verbatim (no findings were in that prose — the passes below hold them, untouched);
and both sessions independently labelled a pass **"L"** for different work, so
theirs is relabelled **L′** while its finding ID `F-L01` is left exactly as its
author wrote it.*

**Thirty passes, A–AD plus L′ and the parallel session's own N. 157 distinct
finding IDs are named in this document**, of which Pass P added 17, Pass Q 12,
and Session 8 (passes U–AD) twelve (plus one earlier ID, C3-S3-02, now cited
individually rather than by range).

*Re-counted 2026-09-19, and the method matters because the number is meant to be
reproducible. An ID is counted when it is NAMED anywhere in this document, which
is the method the 151 figure used:*

```
grep -oE "\b(C[1-4]-S[0-9]+-[0-9]+|C[1-4]-[A-Z][0-9]+|F-[A-Z][0-9]+|F[0-9]+|LB-[0-9]+)\b" \
  finalaudit.md | sort -u | wc -l
```

*That command prints **158**, and exactly one of those is not an ID: `C1-S4`,
matched out of the wildcard reference `C1-S4-*` where Pass P's worker files are
cited (`grep -n 'C1-S4-\*' finalaudit.md` finds it; the line number moves as the
document grows, so it is not quoted here). Hence 157. The
discrepancy is stated rather than hidden in the pattern, because a count whose
command does not reproduce it is the defect this document keeps finding
elsewhere.*

*Two corrections to the instrument itself, both of which it had wrong before:
`M1`/`M23`-style IDs are MILESTONES, not findings, and were being counted as
findings; and `C2-B*`/`C2-M*` were being MISSED entirely, because Claude-2's IDs
do not use the `-S<n>-` form the earlier pattern assumed — so the old figure was
simultaneously too high and too low.*

*The 151 figure below was verified across the merge with `main` rather than
asserted, and that verification stands for the state it described:* 150
IDs here, 99 there, 151 in the union and 151 in the merged file, with none

## The one pattern worth carrying forward

**The failures in this repository are mostly guards that could not see what they
were named for.** A sweep that read one line at a time (Pass C). A probe that
granted itself the privileges it was testing for (`F-015`). A concurrency check
that never ran two things at once (`F-019`). An index test blind to `UNIQUE`.
A migration replay that only ever ran against an empty database (`F-020`).
Three boundary probes that passed while asserting nothing (`G1`). A bucket-drift
check that could not fire for any input (Pass J). A client-scope test that
asserts scope coverage while the whole catalogue ships in the bundle (`N1`).

Pass N added the purest instance yet, and it is not a test at all: **`.focus-ring`
is a focus indicator that never turns off** (`C2-B01`). It fails WCAG 2.4.7 by
being permanently on. No lint rule, no axe check and no unit test in this
repository can express "this class should have been a state variant" — and 202
call sites grew behind that silence. Its companion, `C2-B02`, is the same shape
one level out: axe returned 326 nodes reading *"background could not be
determined due to a background gradient"*, so the product's most important
buttons are precisely the elements its clean report is silent about. **"Zero
violations" is a statement about what the instrument could see.**

Pass O then found the most literal instance in the repository. Elsewhere the
guards were merely hard to trip; `tests/brand-contrast-contract.test.ts` is a
guard **named** for a property it does not evaluate — it checks that a token is
declared and that a class name is unused, and never computes a ratio. Before
Pass O, `grep -rln "0.2126\|luminance" tests/ lib/ scripts/` returned **nothing**:
a repository with a two-theme palette and a cross-platform token contract had no
implementation of the WCAG contrast formula anywhere. The name is what a
reviewer reads (`C1-S3-03`).

Verifying that a guard **fails when it should** is the highest-yield check in
this repository. Break what it protects and confirm it goes red; a guard nobody
has ever seen red is not evidence.

2. ~~**`0237`, `0239` and `0292` never replayed**~~ — **CLOSED 2026-09-14.**
   pgvector installed; 310 migrations applied, 0 failed; the nine spine tables
   audited. See **Pass L**. It found a real gap (`L1`) and, more importantly,
   **refuted one of Pass E's verified-healthy claims** (`L2`) — `anon` does hold
   write privilege on 483 of 491 tables, and the "zero" was an artefact of a
   hand-built test prelude. A wrong clean bill is worse than an unaudited area,
   because it stops the next person looking.
3. **Production was never verified.** Every Pass E finding describes the
   committed migrations replayed **locally**. If `F-001` holds, production may
   not carry even the policies verified correct. *Permanently blocked for agent
   workers: it needs operator credentials.*

- PROD-001 (the largest single gap between this document and production): **none of `0318`-`0338` has been applied.** Sixteen migrations exist as files, replay cleanly from nothing (**349 applied, 0 failed**, re-measured Pass BT) and pass **61 of 61** boundary probes in CI's Database job, which is green on this branch's head — and production's ledger still records only `0001-0003`. Every row below that reads *"fixed by 0322"* or *"closed by 0324"* is fixed **in the repository** and open **in production**, and the paths the Pass BR sweep classified as *defeated* because a migration in the tree closes their source table (`gift_payments`, `pay_handles`, `wallet_goals`, `dashboard_layouts`) are **live**. Applying them is a human action (`docs/PENDING_PROD_MIGRATIONS.md`); `0321` must **not** be applied as written — it needs `create index concurrently`.
- AUTHZ-011 (measured, not estimated, and re-measured today): **248 tables / 719 (table, verb) pairs** still take a write from any household member — a predicate that is nothing but `is_family_member(family_id)`, with no restrictive guard on that verb and no **role-aware** `raise exception` trigger. This supersedes the 251 / 732 recorded through Pass BS: re-run against a database bootstrapped from the current tree, `0333` and `0338` have closed what they closed in between. Re-derive with `docs/audit/role-blind-write-census.sh` rather than trusting either number. It is **not** a defect count. The split is now a script too — `docs/audit/role-blind-write-triage.sh` — because it had only ever been a hand-count in prose: **184** have no manager gate in the application either and are consistent-open by design, **18** have no writer in `app/`, `lib/`, `components/` or `hooks/` (AUTHZ-020), and **46** are suspect because a file that writes them also carries an `isManager` gate. The 46 is a triage list; each needs its call sites read, because a manager-only guard on a feature that genuinely belongs to the member returns 500 to a child (CENSUS-002). **Writing the triage as a script immediately earned it**: the first version carried its own copy of the census query with a looser definition of *bare* and reported **251 where the census reported 248**, wrongly counting `marketplace_listings`, `marketplace_stores` and `notifications` — whose predicates pin a column beyond `is_family_member` (`member_id = marketplace_member_id(family_id)`, `user_id = auth.uid()`) and are role-blind but CONSTRAINED. Two derivations of one number disagreeing by three is CENSUS-001, -002 and -003 happening a fourth time, so the census now holds the CTEs in exactly one place and exposes `--tables`; the triage reads that and does not know how the list is derived. The refactored census emits byte-identical output to the version it replaced, verified by diff.
- E2E-001 — ✅ **FIXED + PASS (re-verified 2026-09-28).** The cause was the test, not the app: `enterCode` pasted the OTP with a paste event that carried no `clipboardData`, so the digit boxes never filled and no `POST /auth/v1/verify` was issued. `9d7a9b8d0` fixed that and made `probe.wait` report what it saw instead of a bare `Expected: true / Received: false`. Evidence: `main`'s CI run [36388529613](https://github.com/NewWorldVenture/Bubaly/actions/runs/36388529613) on `2d6bd78f` passed **1816 / 1816**, with no skips and no retries. `npx playwright test --list` with the CI flags shows all three `phone-auth-http` cases and all 34 `phone-auth-boundaries` cases in that 1816. The six phone-auth unit files (127 tests) pass locally. The history below is kept as it was written.
  - *Original record:* E2E-001 (**inherited from `main`, not this branch's**): the E2E job is red on three `tests/e2e/phone-auth-http.spec.ts` cases. This branch's merge-base **is** `main`'s head (`ad742c2b`, 0 behind / 122 ahead), and `main`'s own CI run on that commit fails **the same three plus a fourth** — 1292 passed / 4 failed there against **1293 passed / 3 failed** here, so this branch is strictly better on E2E than the branch it merges into. `main` went red at `d9542e25` on a different test (`durable-session.spec.ts`, 1251 passed — the phone-auth spec was not executing at all, 41 tests short); `75a1f3c6` *"Keep disposable phone login enabled"* is what made it execute, adding the `/auth/v1/otp` wait and the closed-loopback SMS hook. **Diagnosis**: all three fail in `observeVerify().wait()`, whose poll times out having seen **neither** a route failure **nor a single receipt** — so no `POST /auth/v1/verify` was observed at all and the flow never reached verification. A second, smaller defect hides it: `expect.poll` throws on timeout, so the line below it carrying the only human-readable message is **unreachable in exactly the case that fires**, and CI prints `Expected: true / Received: false`, which names nothing. A patch that makes the failure report what it saw is proposed on the PR and deliberately **not** pushed here — it is a file this branch does not touch, and widening a PR into someone else's red is how a diff stops being reviewable. No re-run was spent: the base branch failing identically is stronger evidence than a re-run would be, and "flake" is not a root cause. **Corroborated independently by the Codex cycle, which found the same three first and diagnosed them better.** Its production-rollout record for release `2a5e7e7a` states: *"E2E105970089707 fails only its three new phone HTTP cases: 1,293/1,296 pass in 8.3 minutes; each stalls before code-entry heading after Continue, so real OTP verification is not reached"*, and *"New hosted phone acceptance remains open"*. That is the same count, the same three cases, and a sharper cause than the one derived here from the logs alone — it says **where** the flow stops (the UI never reaches the code-entry heading), which is exactly what "no `POST /auth/v1/verify` was ever observed" implies without being able to name. So this is **not a new finding and not this branch's**: it is a known, tracked, pre-existing item already owned under **AUTH-001 / AUTH-002 / AUTH-003**, recorded here only because the check is red on this PR and a red check must never be left unexplained. The diagnostic patch proposed on the PR stands on its own merit — it would have made this failure name itself rather than print `Expected: true / Received: false` — and is offered to whoever picks up the phone acceptance work, not pushed here. **CORRECTION (2026-09-20): the Codex cause this row called "sharper" is WRONG, and this row's own log-derived reading was right.** *"Each stalls before code-entry heading after Continue"* cannot be what happens, and the spec proves it rather than argues it: `requestCode` carries **its own two assertions before it returns** — `expect(await sent, 'Disposable GoTrue must accept the configured test-number OTP request').toEqual({ status: 200, errorCode: null })` and `await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Enter the code we sent you' })).toBeVisible()`. If the flow stalled before code entry **that** assertion would fail. It passes; the reported line is `:129`, inside `probe.wait`, which is reached only *after* `enterCode`. So GoTrue accepts the OTP, the code-entry screen renders, and what never happens is the `POST /auth/v1/verify` — exactly what this row derived from the logs before deferring. **The lesson is the one CENSUS-004 recorded**: a second agent's account was accepted as better-informed without being checked against the source, and it was the less accurate of the two. **The component path was then traced and reads as sound**, which narrows the search usefully rather than closing it: `otp-input.tsx:78-85` calls `onChange(pasted)` then `onComplete?.(pasted)` in one event; `phone-auth.tsx:99-105` `changeCode` calls `retire()` — clearing `busy.current` — and assigns `intent.current.code` **synchronously** before `setCode`, which is what the comment at `:147` says it is for; and `lib/auth/otp.ts:7,12` give `normalizeOtp('000000') === '000000'` with `isValidOtp` true. So neither the `busy.current` guard nor the `token !== intent.current.code` guard rejects the first deliberately-wrong code, and `verify()` should reach the network. **A one-assertion patch that decides it in a single run is proposed on the PR** — assert `Digit 1` and `Digit 6` hold their pasted values between `enterCode` and `probe.wait`: empty means the synthetic paste never reaches React and the defect is in the harness; filled means `verify()` is entered and something past the guards swallows the request. **Not pushed**, because Docker is unavailable here so `supabase start` cannot run and a patch to auth code that cannot be executed once is a guess. The determinism is itself evidence for the second branch: three runs here and three on `main`, all failing identically, is not a race.
- SEO-001: Both generated social preview images answer 307 to /login for an unauthenticated crawler, so no shared Bubaly link renders a preview card on any platform.
- SEO-002: resolveMarketingMetadata replaces the root Open Graph object with {title, description}, deleting og:image, og:url, og:type and og:site_name from every marketing page.

- SEO-003: Eight of the eleven published marketing page families answered 307 to /login for anonymous visitors and search engines; the middleware now derives its public prefixes from PAGE_TYPES instead of restating them.
- SEO-004: /pay/<handle>, the Pay-ID resolver a relative follows to send a gift, answered 307 to /login while the /gift/<token> link it forwards to answered 200 — the fifth route in this audit whose only caller is unauthenticated, sitting behind the session boundary.
- DATA-008: Eighteen useRealtimeQuery call sites across fourteen files rendered an empty state for a failed read — "No bills yet" on a failed bills query, a rewards balance computed from reads that failed, "Nothing on the horizon" from the page whose job is to say what is coming. All 231 call sites are now swept by a guard that requires each to surface its error or be named, with a reason, as deliberately silent.
- DATA-009: logAudit's try/catch could never fire — PostgREST resolves with { data, error } rather than throwing, so the line written to notice a failed audit write had never run, and all fourteen callers lost their audit rows silently. Ten wallet-audit writes discarded the error the same way, including the credit and debit paths.
- DATA-009 (sharpest instance): the Guardian escalation route set pushSent = true on the line after that insert, inside the try — so a refused write still recorded push_sent = true in the guardian_escalations row and returned it to the caller. An emergency was recorded as having alerted the parents when nothing was written.

Reconciled 2026-09-27 (PORT-001 follow-up): waits on an owner decision (which voting model is canonical); this ledger counts only credential and provider rows as BLOCKED, so it stays IN PROGRESS until that decision is made. **Pass AR re-diagnosis: the database constraint the upstream narrative asked for would be a regression.** Two surfaces run different voting rules on the same `meal_vote_ballots`. `/dashboard/recipes/vote` rates EACH option yes/maybe/no (`castBallot` upserts on `(option_id, member_id)`, scored by `lib/recipes/voting.ts` `tallyVotes`), which is what 0055's `UNIQUE (option_id, member_id)` encodes. The meals planner card is single-choice: it deletes all the member's ballots on the vote, then inserts one yes. `UNIQUE (vote_id, member_id)` would make the ratings page fail on a member's second option. Fixed now, because it is wrong under either model: the planner card counted every ballot as support, so a 👎 cast on the ratings page raised that meal's bar and marked it as the viewer's pick. It now counts only `yes` over distinct members (`yesShares`), which gives identical numbers on its own single-choice ballots. Still open, and the owner's call: voting in the planner erases the member's ratings on every other option of that vote. To close, choose (a) single choice everywhere, then migrate to `UNIQUE (vote_id, member_id)` and make the ratings page single-choice; or (b) ratings everywhere, then make the planner card cast a rating instead of clearing. |

The single consolidated audit of bubaly.com. Sections 1–19 are the consolidated
view; **Part II** below is the evidence, kept verbatim, pass by pass.

**How this file is built.** Four workers audit in parallel and each writes only
its own file under `audit/`. Claude-1 merges them here and is the only account
that writes to this file. Worker findings are merged, deduplicated, and cited
back to the worker that found them; nothing verified is ever dropped on a
rebuild.

| worker | area | source file |
|---|---|---|
| Claude-1 | coordinator · architecture · integrations | `audit/claude-1.md` |
| Claude-2 | frontend · UI/UX · responsive · accessibility | `audit/claude-2.md` |
| Claude-3 | backend · API · database · auth · security | `audit/claude-3.md` |
| Claude-4 | QA · features · flows · performance · edge cases | `audit/claude-4.md` |

**The rule this audit is built on:** nothing closes on reasoning. A finding
closes when a command, a probe, a replayed database or a rendered page
demonstrates it — and wherever a fix is claimed, the check was also run against
the *broken* state to prove it was not passing vacuously. That discipline has
caught nine defects in this audit's own instruments, four of them found only by
deliberately breaking the thing being guarded.

---

# 1. Executive Summary

Fifteen passes (A–O) over fifteen surfaces, plus the four-worker parallel
audit now running. **63 named findings from the passes, and counting from the
workers.** The codebase
is in good structural health; the defects cluster in one recognisable shape.

**The shape.** Nearly every serious finding here is the same defect wearing
different clothes: **a control that is real on the screen and absent behind it.**

- Family Autopilot was a Plus feature on the sidebar and ran nightly for every
  family on the platform (**F15**).
- 24 of 62 paid features were enforced by a padlock icon; the URL was the bypass
  (**F16**).
- 20 endpoints behind feature-gated pages had no entitlement check — the `fetch`
  was the bypass, mostly on the surface that costs money per call (**F18**).
- A child could clear the family chore board, mint chores for a sibling, and
  self-approve a reward (**F20**, **F21**) — manager-only on the screen, nothing
  underneath.
- The AI Assistant page was gated at `basic` while the published Free plan sells
  it, *and* `/api/ai` behind it had no plan check at all — the gate backwards on
  both halves at once (**L-01**, **L-03**).
- The password vault demands step-up MFA on the page, and no policy in the schema
  references `aal` (**O-03**); a child could read, change and delete the family's
  stored card PIN (**O-01**).

**The second shape** is silence: a write whose result is discarded, followed by
something claiming it happened. Eight in Pass C, plus **E-01**, **F-a**, **F-b**.
`logAudit`'s `catch` block could never run, so every caller lost audit rows and
nothing said so. An emergency escalation recorded `push_sent: true` for a
notification that was never written.

**What is genuinely strong.** RLS is on for all 491 tables with no blanket
policy (**Pass G**). Every export of every `'use server'` module authenticates
its caller (**Pass D**, 0 findings). No `readOnly` AI tool can write (**Pass J**,
0 findings). No server secret is reachable from the browser bundle (**Pass N**,
0 findings). The money tables carry three manager-gated restrictive write guards
and survive a concurrency probe. 310 migrations replay clean; 20 behavioural
probes pass in CI.

**What is left, and whose it is.** Nine items, none of them a code defect this
audit can close: the production migration ledger (**F5**/**F-001**) needs a
credentialed operator; **F6** needs config; **F19**'s remaining 35 unmetered AI
routes, **O-02**'s credential reads and **SEC-001**'s public media bucket are
product decisions; migrations `0296` and `0297` are authored, replay clean, and
deliberately **not applied** to production.

---

# 2. Critical Issues

| id | finding | state |
|---|---|---|
| **O-01** | A child could read, change and delete the family's stored card PIN. `family_credentials` allows categories `card` and `pin`, stores `secret` as plain text, and all four policies were `is_family_member`. Proved: a `child` on an `aal1` session READ the PIN, UPDATED it, DELETED the row. | **Fixed** — `0297`, **not applied to production** |
| **I-01** | A social restriction could be removed by the person it restricted. Deleting the override row restores the higher default, returning `publish_posts` to someone a parent deliberately stopped. | **Fixed** — `0296`, **not applied to production** |
| **S-01** | **A guest could accept an invite as a parent.** `invites_update` was created with a `USING` clause and **no `WITH CHECK`**; Postgres then reuses `USING` as the write check, and that clause's invitee branch constrains exactly one column — `email`. So the invited person could rewrite `family_id` and `role` on their own row, and `accept_invite()` (SECURITY DEFINER) copies both straight into `family_members`. Found by **Claude-3**, reproduced end to end by Claude-1: a babysitter invited as `guest` issued one `update invites set role='parent'`, accepted through the ordinary flow, and **joined the household as a parent**. No second family, no guessed UUID — the `family_id` is in her own invite row, which `invites_select` lets her read. `authenticated` holds UPDATE on the table by Supabase's default privileges, so it is one PostgREST PATCH with no app code involved. | **Fixed** — `0298`, **not applied to production** |
| **Q-01** | **A child's spendable balance was totalled from part of the ledger, and spends raced.** `bucketBalanceCents` fetched the whole `wallet_transactions` history over PostgREST with **no bound** and reduced it in JavaScript. PostgREST caps at `db-max-rows`, so on a busy bucket it totalled the first page — **Claude-4 measured $92.00 reported against a real $40.00** on 1,052 rows. It also read-then-inserted with no lock: **two simultaneous $8 spends against $10 both posted, balance −$6.00**. Six other money operations go through locking RPCs; this was the one spend path that did not, and `requestSpendAction`'s own docstring says *"Never overdraws"*. | **Fixed + PASS, both halves, and the race is now provable on demand.** The read was paged first (deployable, no migration). The race needed an RPC and now has one: `0342_a_child_cannot_spend_the_same_dollar_twice.sql` adds `wallet_debit_spend_bucket`, which takes the spend bucket's row lock, totals `completed` + `processing` INSIDE it, refuses an overdraw, writes the debit and the `wallet_audit_logs` row in the SAME transaction, and returns the decision. `debitSpendBucket` in `lib/wallet/server.ts` calls it instead of read-then-insert; `bucketBalanceCents` stays for DISPLAY and no longer decides anything — a balance read outside the lock is a memory by the time the insert is sent. **A second defect fell out of the same change**: the RPC totals `processing` as well as `completed`, so a live card hold is no longer invisible to an in-app spend. **NOT APPLIED** — `0342` is the owner's, like `0318`–`0341`, and is recorded in `docs/PENDING_PROD_MIGRATIONS.md`. **Proved, not asserted.** `docs/audit/a-child-cannot-spend-the-same-dollar-twice-check.sql` races two simultaneous $8 spends against $10 on separate connections and requires exactly one to post, $8.00 debited, $2.00 left, the loser refused with `insufficient_funds` and `available=200`. Its **negative control** puts the read-then-insert shape back and requires the overdraft to reproduce: **2 of 2 approved, bucket at −$6.00, $16.00 debited** — the exact figure this row was filed with, on demand. **The probe had to be fixed before it could be trusted, and the fix is the same lesson `AUDIT-005` just learned.** As first written it synchronised the racers with an advisory starting gate and then asserted their clock spans intersected. Stress-tested at **1 failure in 10** under six competing workers, with both racers provably parked at the gate and their spans still disjoint — because being GRANTED a lock is not being SCHEDULED. That would have been a flaky-red money boundary in CI, which is `AUDIT-004`'s habit arriving from the other side. The assertion was moved off the clock entirely: a third session holds `for update` on the bucket row, both racers run until they queue on it, and `pg_locks` is polled until both are waiting. **12 of 12 under the load that broke the old one 1 in 10.** **And the claim written about that assertion was itself too strong, which is recorded rather than quietly corrected.** Both probes' comments said the waiter count is a DIRECT test of the RPC's `for update` — remove the lock and nobody queues. **False, and measured false**: the negative-control stage still reports `contended=2`, because an INSERT into `wallet_transactions` takes **FOR KEY SHARE** on the `wallet_buckets` row its `bucket_id` references, which conflicts with the holder's FOR UPDATE. Verified directly — holding the bucket row in one session and issuing a plain INSERT in another blocks the INSERT. So the waiter count proves the two racers were in flight together, which is exactly what the clock spans could not show, and nothing more; the guard removal is caught by the outcome assertions and the negative control. The same overstatement was written into `wallet-concurrency-check.sql` an hour earlier and is corrected there too |
| **U-01** | **The family calendar put every event on the wrong day outside UTC.** Day columns were keyed from a *local-midnight* `Date` through `toISOString()`; events from their true instant, also through `toISOString()`. Those agree only at offset zero. Found by **Claude-2**, replayed by Claude-1: in `Europe/Amsterdam` and `Asia/Tokyo` **0 of 7** days matched their own column and the seventh day's events keyed to a date no column carried, so they **did not render at all**; in `America/New_York` events from 21:00 and in `America/Los_Angeles` from 19:00 landed a column late. Six of the eleven shipped locales are UTC+1/+2. | **Fixed** — `lib/time/local-day.ts` + 19 guard cases |

**All three fixes are authored, replay clean, and are gated behind F5. Until the
ledger is repaired, all three defects are live in production** — and S-01 is a
remote privilege escalation to parent of a household, reachable by anyone who
holds a pending invite.

### The correction S-01 forces on this audit

**Pass I examined this exact policy and recorded it as *"exactly right"*:**

> | `invites` | `can_manage_family`, plus an update clause letting the invited person accept their **own** invite by matching their JWT email | exactly right |

That row is wrong, and the reason it is wrong is worth more than the row. Pass I
read the `USING` clause and asked whether its *predicate* was correct. It never
asked whether `WITH CHECK` was **present**. An absent clause has no text to
read, so a review that reads policy expressions cannot see it — and the whole of
Pass I was conducted that way.

`docs/audit/invite-cannot-rewrite-what-it-grants-check.sql` closes it
behaviourally and pins the structural cause: a `w`-command policy with
`polwithcheck IS NULL` fails the probe, whatever its `USING` says. The same
question should be asked of every other UPDATE policy in the schema — recorded
as the next task in `audit/claude-1.md`.

What it does establish is that the repair is **not a config line** — every React-resolving path must move together, transitive dependencies included — and that until it does, the suite's green is evidence about React 18 while production renders under a 19 canary. It could not be guarded under the rule this audit keeps (guard only what every path reaches behind the step-up): a dozen surfaces outside the vault read sensitive rows with no way to enter a code — the home dashboard's expiring passports, licences and insurance, the command centre, readiness, planning, household search, and the chat assistant, which signs file URLs — so a silent RLS filter would turn "your passport expires in three weeks" into "nothing expiring". Three decisions are the owner's: **(D1)** ask enrolled managers for the code at sign-in (after which every step-up guard is free), teach each surface to say "private documents hidden", or accept that reads stay a page gate; **(D2)** what `/dashboard/home`'s Remove and asset delete may do to a vaulted document (the asset delete cascades through `documents.asset_id` and bypasses RLS, so it needs a trigger or an FK change, not a policy); **(D3)** how to guard stored files with no documents row (insurance cards, tax-vault uploads), which need a folder rule. The category-scoped guard is written and ready once D1 and D2 are decided. **The history follows, unchanged.** **Open — but no longer blocked on the design, which Pass BT measured end to end.** Pass O recorded the obstacle correctly: `requireAal2` deliberately does **not** step up a family that never enrolled a factor, so a policy demanding `auth.jwt()->>'aal' = 'aal2'` would lock every factor-less family out of their own vault, and the right mirror is *"aal2, **or** this user has no enrolled factor"* — needing a `security definer` helper over `auth.mfa_factors`. **That is right, and Pass BT demonstrated why the helper is not optional rather than leaving it as a preference:** a policy subquery executes as the **invoking** role, and `authenticated` holds no grant on `auth.mfa_factors`, so the bare `not exists (select 1 from auth.mfa_factors …)` form fails **`permission denied for table mfa_factors`** for every real user. **The predicate was then run on a bootstrapped database, four cases with a negative control**, against `public.bills` as a stand-in, all inside a rolled-back transaction: (A) no enrolled factor at `aal1` → **1 row** — *the factor-less family is not locked out, which is the whole objection this row recorded*; (B) a verified TOTP factor enrolled, same `aal1` session → **0 rows**, refused; (C) same session at `aal2` → **1 row**, restored; (D) **negative control** — drop the guard and repeat B exactly → **1 row**, so B was refused by the guard and not by something else. The shim now creates a minimal `auth.mfa_factors`, for the reason it already gives itself about `storage.objects` (*"otherwise storage isolation is untestable — policies inert"*). An outside person following the Pay ID they were given for one child lands on a gift link for another — and the child needs to mint nothing, because `0322` already closed `gift_links`; they repoint the handle at a link that exists. `is_active = false` or a `DELETE` is the denial-of-service variant | **Pass BQ** | **Fixed by `0324` (UNAPPLIED).** The service-role read is correct and stays — a public payment page cannot carry the visitor's session — which is exactly why the row it trusts must be manager-written |
