- The hints and the photo-or-video prompt are four new keys in all seven catalogues, written in each locale's existing voice for this form.
- The difficulty uses the `missionsNew.*` keys the new-mission form already labels it with.

The i18n ratchet (`tests/i18n-ungated-surface-ratchet.test.ts`) counts the literals that are gone.

**P-34 · Medium · A child's wallet and the wallet's activity page spoke English to every family.** Found while retesting DATA-023 (2026-09-28) with the reader's language set to German.

`/wallet/children/[childId]` showed, in every language:
- "saved" in the balance line;
- "Target: 40% …" under the split donut, glued from sentence fragments, and "Target 40%" on each bucket;
- "Ask AI Money Coach" and "Thinking…";
- each ledger row's type ("Top-up", "Transfer") and its time, "Today, 11:44 AM", from the en-US-bound `fmtRelative`;
- the card-spend trust badges (Auto, Allowed, Policy, Delegated, Emergency);
- the two toasts after a spend request.

`/wallet/activity` listed every type, the "All types" filter and every non-completed status in English. The wallet's section tabs (Overview, Treasury, Send, Goals and the rest) were English on all 23 wallet pages. And every top-up the page made was stored with the description "Parent top-up", which then titled the row in every language.

Fixed:
- 46 keys in all seven catalogues. The split line is one template with four holes, not English glued to fragments.
- The section tabs are a named `<nav>`, and the current tab carries `aria-current`.
- Row times come from `useFormat()`, in the reader's language and clock.
- Types and statuses come from `walletTxn.*`. The English label stays only as the fallback for a value no key names, and for the statement export.
- A top-up made without a description now stores none, so its row reads as "Aufladung", "Recarga" and so on. Rows already written keep the English text they were stored with.

The scanner saw almost none of these: JSX text after an expression, and labels held in a map outside the component. `tests/the-wallet-ledger-speaks-the-readers-language.test.ts` fails 4 of 6 on the previous code. It checks that every type, status and tab has a key in every complete catalogue.

**P-35 · Medium · With the Family Wallet active, two wallet pages failed axe.** Found by axe on the wallet routes after the MAIN-F-J07 retest had activated the persona family's wallet (2026-09-28). B14's crawl ran before that, when every wallet route showed the activation screen. So it measured that screen, not the pages.
- `/wallet/send`: the back arrow was an icon-only link with no name (`link-name`, serious).
- `/wallet/activity` had no `<h1>`. The view's title was an `<h2>`, and the page's only `<h1>` was on the activation screen it shows when the wallet is off.
- The static guards passed both. `unnamedIconButtons` looked only at buttons, and the heading guard counts an `<h1>` anywhere in a page's imports.

Fixed:
- The back link is named ("Back to Wallet") and the activity title is the `<h1>`.
- The icon-only scan now covers `<a>` and `<Link>`. On the wider scan it found one more: the external-link icon on the admin feedback page's notifications, now named. A lone child carrying `alt` or `label` names its link, which clears the six false positives the wider scan raised (a photo with `alt`, and a stat pill with a text label).
- `tests/every-signed-in-page-has-a-heading.test.ts` asserts that each wallet view draws its own `<h1>`.
- Re-run with the wallet active, axe finds 0 violations and exactly one `<h1>` on all 12 wallet routes, as the parent and as the teen (24 loads).

**P-36 · Low · A member with no display name was greeted "Good afternoon, .", and four greetings fell back to the English word "there".** Found while driving a fresh local account for the MAIN-F-M01 retest (2026-09-28).
- **The dashboard:** it built the name as `display_name ?? email-prefix ?? 'there'`, and `??` lets an empty string through. So an account whose display name is `''` read "Good afternoon, .".
- **English fallbacks:** `/home`, the personal dashboard, the marketplace assistant and a dead line in the concierge module fell back to the literal `'there'`. That overrode `roleGreeting`'s own translated fallback ("zusammen" in German), and the marketplace assistant said "Hi {name}" in English, glued to a sentence fragment.

Fixed:
- An empty name is no name. The dashboard greeting then drops the name instead of printing an empty one.
- The other surfaces pass an empty name to `roleGreeting`, which uses the catalogue's word.
- The marketplace greeting is one sentence per language, with and without a name, in all seven catalogues. The old fragment key is removed.
- `tests/a-greeting-without-a-name-has-none.test.ts` fails 3 of 3 on the previous code. It also forbids `?? 'there'` and `|| 'there'` anywhere in `app/` and `components/`.
- Retested on a production build with the parent's display name blanked, then restored:
  - `/dashboard` and `/home` fall back to the account's email prefix ("Good afternoon, bubaly-personas+parent1."), in English and German, where the dashboard had read "Good afternoon, .";
  - the marketplace assistant says "Hi! Ask me prices…" and "Hallo! Fragen Sie mich…".

### B15 — the adult, the teen, the caregiver and the guest: every control and every form

*session_01TRY21ZKsFrfB3qtoP972A4, claimed 11:10Z (#633), run 2026-09-28 11:10–15:00Z.* B6 pressed everything as a parent, B11 as a PIN child; B7 only rendered a teen. This batch signs in one member of each remaining role, each through `/login` with an email, in the same Family+ household on a local production build of main `2d6bd78f`, with migrations through `0461` applied.

| Pass | Adult | Teen | Caregiver | Guest |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Render, 1280 px, every signed-in route | 350; 272 reached | 350; 270 reached | 350; 270 reached | 350; 270 reached |
| Every control (`--interact`) on the routes reached | 269 routes, 1,265 clicks | 268, 1,167 | 268 | 268, 1,171 |
| Every form (`--submit`) | 113 forms: 111 answered, 6 refused by the browser (P-40) | 94: 88 answered, 5 refused by the app, 5 by the browser | 94: 87 answered, 6 by the app, 5 by the browser | 94: 84 answered, 6 by the app, 5 by the browser |
| Direct writes with the session's own token (role, rename, invite a parent, plan, family, a bill) | self-promotion and the parent invite written (owner decision, above) | all refused | all refused | all refused |

"Refused by the app" is always a manager-only write offered to a non-manager, answered in words: "You don't have permission to do that. Ask a family admin if you think this is a mistake." That applies to Add bill (bills, autopay, due), Add Entry (passwords) and Add subscription (0460). The refusal is correct. Whether a teen, caregiver or guest should be offered those forms at all is ROLE-SCOPE-001's and PROD-002's question. One caregiver "Add bill" recorded no message because the toast had gone by the time the crawler read it; by hand it shows for three seconds.

A first run of the submission pass reused sessions saved three hours earlier. Their refresh tokens had already been rotated by the interaction pass, so every page answered as signed out. That run was discarded and repeated with fresh sessions, and every row above was signed in.

**What each role reaches.** All four render 350 of 350 signed-in routes with no page error. The adult reaches 272 (every family route, and `/dashboard/family-access`); the teen, caregiver and guest reach the same 270 family routes and are sent from `/dashboard/family-access` to `/home`. Every `/admin` route sends all four to `/dashboard`. The redirect arrives mid-stream, so a crawler can catch the address before it changes. The check that matters: the HTML and the RSC payload of `/admin/users`, fetched as the guest, teen, adult and caregiver, never contain another family's email, while the super admin's copy of the same page does.

**PUSH-007, found independently.** The interaction pass's server log showed "Push dispatch failed: Error: Push cursor write failed" from `/api/notifications/generate` on every run after the first. The cause was the push cursor's compare-and-set: `.eq('value', stored.value)` sent a JSON object as the text `[object Object]`, and Postgres refused it with 22P02, so a family received its first batch of push notifications and none after. This batch had a field-by-field fix ready (`value->>id`, `value->>createdAt`) and confirmed the defect on the real local database. Another session found the same defect and fixed it first as **PUSH-007** (#644, sending the stored cursor as JSON text). Main's fix was kept and this one dropped, so there is one fix. The local reproduction adds a data point for PUSH-007: the old guard answers `22P02 invalid input syntax for type json` against a real PostgREST, and a run holding a stale cursor still loses the claim after the fix.

**P-37 · Medium · "Analyze my finances" was silent when it was refused.** The teen, caregiver and guest each pressed it on `/dashboard/subscriptions`. `/api/ai/savings` correctly refused them with 403 and a translated reason (API-SWEEP-05). The card read only `summary` and `suggestions`, so the spinner stopped and nothing appeared. An engine that is not set up (503) was silent the same way. Fixed: the card shows the route's own message in an alert. It falls back to the catalogue's "temporarily unavailable" rather than an English literal. The answer is read by a pure function, `readSavingsAnswer`. `tests/a-refused-savings-analysis-says-so.test.ts` has 5 cases, all failing on the previous card.

**P-38 · Low · The App Lock card and an event's RSVP list showed a failed read as the raw error.** Found by the MAIN-F-J04 retest (2026-09-28), which aborted the App Lock settings read in a browser with the lock configured.
- **What held:** the card no longer offered "Set up PIN" over the configured lock, which is the finding's fix.
- **What it showed instead:** after the client's four retries (about eight seconds), the card printed "TypeError: Failed to fetch". It did the same in German.
- **The RSVP list:** an event's RSVP list printed PostgREST's own error text the same way.

Fixed:
- Both show a message from the catalogue, written in each locale's voice for that screen. The App Lock message says the PIN has not changed.
- The raw error stays in the `title` attribute and the server log.
- `tests/a-read-failure-is-said-in-the-readers-language.test.ts` fails 2 of 3 on the previous code.
- Retested in English and German, with and without the network failure: the alert reads "Couldn't check App Lock right now…" / "App Lock konnte gerade nicht geprüft werden…", and with the network working the card offers "Turn on" / "Einschalten".
- The admin pages and the per-page "some details unavailable" panels still show raw text on purpose, as diagnostics.

**P-39 · Medium · The notes grid card and the recipe card were one button with buttons inside.** Found by the MAIN-F-D06 retest (2026-09-28), which seeded a note and ran axe on `/dashboard/notes`: `nested-interactive`, serious.
- **The cause:** both cards were `role="button"` and held their own controls (open, pin and delete; open and favourite). A button's children are presentational, so assistive technology was told to ignore the inner buttons.
- **How it happened:** MAIN-F-D06's fix had moved each card's keyboard control onto a real inner `<button>`, and the notes card's own comment says the card "must not take role=button". A merge kept both.
- **Why B14 missed it:** the persona family had no notes or recipes, so its crawl never rendered either card.

Fixed:
- The cards are `role="presentation"`, with the click kept for the mouse. Their title `<button>` is the control.
- A new scan (`nestedInteractive` in `tests/helpers/jsx-a11y-scan.ts`) checks the whole tree. It found exactly these two, plus two drop zones whose file input is hidden and so takes no focus. `tests/a-button-holds-no-other-control.test.ts` holds it at zero and fails on the previous cards.
- Retested with a note and a recipe present: axe finds 0 violations on both pages. By keyboard alone, 7 and 12 Tabs land on the real title buttons and Enter opens each item.

**P-40 · Medium · A money field refused the exact amount.** The browser refused the submission pass on the same fields for every role, the adult included. A number input rejects any value that is not a multiple of its `step`, and thirteen money fields carried a coarse one, so the form would not submit:
- a mover's quote of $1,875 or a move's spend (step 50 and 10);
- a salary target or range of $65,432 (step 100);
- a project's budget, labour or quote of $125 (step 10);
- a plan's budget (step 10);
- a Trust rule's maximum amount and the wallet's approval threshold of $12 (step 5);
- a babysitter payment of $60.25 in the field labelled "Or enter exact amount" (step 0.5).

Every one is stored in cents, and every parser already keeps cents (`Math.round(n * 100)`). Fixed: all thirteen take `step="0.01"`, and each now asks a phone for the decimal keypad (`inputMode="decimal"`), which the M-006 guard requires of a decimal field. Minutes, a radius in metres, the investment sliders and reward points keep their deliberate increments. `tests/a-money-field-takes-the-exact-amount.test.ts` scans `components/` and `app/` for money-named number inputs and named all thirteen on the previous code.

**Seen and not defects.**
- `/api/ai/*` answered 503 "not configured" on a dozen pages: the local stack has no AI key.
- The library's `/library/media/<id>` answered 415 for a book whose audio link was a web page (synthetic data from an earlier form pass). The route refuses non-audio, and the player says "That audio could not be played."
- Social connect's "Add (setup)" answered 500 for the teen, caregiver and guest. That is the refused social permission, which P-24 already turns into "That wasn't saved · Your account can't make that change".
- A single ChunkLoadError on `/dashboard/weekly-briefing` for the caregiver passed on a re-render.

**Recorded for the owner, not changed:** the adult's self-promotion and the `parent` invite path (added to the SEC-026 owner decision above), and ROLE-SCOPE-001 (guest and caregiver scope, and the permission matrix), both merged in #638.

Invitation is email: manager creation is RLS-gated and rate-limited by family, but the send endpoint lacks per-invite reservation/idempotency. `API-1AC88B3A7ED8` remains open. Marketing SMS is draft-only under `ACTION-3C20B106C849`; current evidence does not establish consent enforcement or real sending. No runtime repro, provider calls, credentials or edits were used; the Guardian workflow remains open.

Weekly meal-planning review and independent peer review both keep `MEAL-001` IN PROGRESS. The flow has family-scoped reads/writes, same-family database guards, controlled React/browser tests and a historical hosted single-family journey; these do not prove live multi-family RLS through the UI or real concurrent Postgres behavior. `SERVICE-37FEFA156D44` (IP/Medium), supported by `SERVICE-78FB7849C3BC` (`setSlot`, NS), `SERVICE-38A29C9F4697` (`removeSlot`, NS), `API-023`, `MOD-060`, `ACT-071` and `PAGE-192`: `lib/services/meals/index.ts:396+` performs snapshot, delete, insert, readback and compensation as separate operations, without a transaction or unique `(family_id,plan_date,meal_type)` constraint. At `:457–488`, compensation restores snapshot rows when a slot is empty; a concurrent remover can therefore have its deletion undone after the original delete returns fewer rows (`:502–508`) and compensation runs. Existing `tests/service-meals.test.ts:298–310` protects a newer competing row after insert failure, not concurrent deletion; the duplicate-slot browser test injects a competing row in a fake rather than exercising two Postgres writers. This is a source-derived scenario, not an executed repro; next evidence should be a deterministic disposable-DB two-writer interleaving test. Second, `components/modules/meals-module.tsx:789–822` retains an AI-plan receipt only after HTTP response; if `planWeek` commits but the reply is lost, retry can call `/api/ai/meals/plan` again and replace the saved week because the route has no request idempotency key. Test commit-with-lost-response and establish idempotency/readback before claiming retry safety. PR #864 is an OPEN draft based on #797 and changes navigation labels only; merged #846’s receipt guard covers neither boundary. No data/runtime changes or row status/closure changes.

PR #879 remains OPEN+DRAFT at `260cb89c8575d83b25a28fe67881c2198e764e4f`, stacked on #866. Its bounded Todo completion guard has 24 focused and 49 default tests passing plus scoped lint and strict types, but hosted CI is red/pending: Mobile dependency audit fails on the still-reachable braces@3.0.3 advisory, Main Typecheck/Lint/Test/Build is now failed with logs unavailable until the run completes, and E2E is pending; Database/RLS and preview-comment checks pass. Keep it draft; no merge/production claim. Counts/statuses/closures are unchanged; production readiness remains NO.

## #834 exact-head release gate review — 2026-10-04 02:24 UTC

Exact head: `2fa2afb566791e6ca98dc243eb38d7e4221e2ded`. GitHub reports all required and auxiliary checks successful, including E2E; PR remains open, non-draft, with no submitted review. Green CI does not cover these independently reproduced database cases:

- **Family-history privacy:** migration 0475 lines 21–26 sets `is_family_chat` based on the currently active roster. `messaging_private.can_access_conversation` lines 28–34 then grants all active family members access when that flag is true. A subgroup excluding an inactive member can be promoted; reactivating that member exposes old messages and attachments. Exact-head SQL remains unchanged from the prior synthetic PG17 reproduction.
- **Revocation ordering:** `messaging_private.message_guard()` checks `family_members.is_active` without a row lock, and the insert policy does not serialize against deactivation. Prior two-session PG17 reproduction shows a pending message insert can commit after deactivation commits. Lock membership in a mode conflicting with the `is_active` update and cover both serial orders.
- **Migration compatibility:** PR discussion reports production `notifications.related_id` remains UUID and expected sender/read triggers are absent; target migration ledger/catalog is not accessible here. Editing historical 0293 will not repair a database that already recorded it. Verify the target ledger/catalog and provide forward migrations for missing changes before release. #834 and #890 both allocate version 0475; select one owner and perform combined numeric replay. Check public `family-media` URL consumers before making that bucket private.

The findings and exact requested regressions were published without branch edits in [the #834 review follow-up](https://github.com/NewWorldVenture/Bubaly/pull/834#issuecomment-5975742846). A new local successor is being prepared from #834 to address the two privacy/order defects; it is not pushed.

## #834 independent review follow-up — 2026-10-04 02:46 UTC

Review of `e711797cdba671401362efca4afccd74d66590cc` found the migration's exact-roster check fail-closed for inactive members, NULLs and duplicates, and `FOR SHARE` correctly orders send inserts against `is_active` updates.
